Senses.Explanation: Go drink tea is an ordinary imperative made famous by Zhaozhou Congshen's public exchange with two visitors and the temple steward. Later records raise, question, quote, and comment on those same words as a named case while leaving the command itself concrete. One says no and the other yes; Zhaozhou gives both the same words. When the temple steward asks why, Zhaozhou calls, 'Steward!'; after the steward answers, Zhaozhou again says, 'Go drink tea.' Independent records reverse the order of the two visitors but retain the same public exchange, and a later retelling writes 'drink' with the alternate graph. The phrase then remains available as a live answer in other public interviews: Zifu Zhensui answers a question about 'three-by-three in front and three-by-three behind' by asking the questioner's name and then saying it; Daweishan Cheng gives it as his response for receiving a guest and rejects the questioner's easy equation of him with Zhaozhou; and Baizhang Daoheng gives it immediately when the assembly gathers, beside the separate formulas 'take care' and 'rest.' Foyan Qingyuan explicitly says that he usually says 'go drink tea' and says it again that day. It also becomes the named allusion 'Zhaozhou's tea,' paired in a verse with 'Yunmen's flatbread.' The Zen bend is public deployment: an ordinary imperative is preserved as Zhaozhou's repeatable interview formula, questioned inside its originating exchange, then quoted, alluded to, and spoken anew by later masters while retaining the same literal wording.
Senses.Note: The headword occurs 781 times across 170 allowlisted texts; the spelling variant with the alternate graph for 'drink' occurs 14 times across 7 texts. The witnesses support one sense: originating case, later answer, assembly dismissal, and allusion are deployments of the same imperative, not different things. The occurrence speaker is the person who actually says the phrase, even when a longer KWIC contains interlocutor turns.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問二新到上座曾到此間否云不曾到師云喫茶去又問那一人曾到此間否云曾到師云喫茶去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), in Zhaozhou Congshen's recorded sayings: Zhaozhou asks both newly arrived monks the question and speaks the exact imperative after each answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問新到。曾到此間麼。曰。曾到。師曰。喫茶去。又問僧。僧曰。不曾到。師曰。喫茶去。後院主問曰。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元), in Zhaozhou Congshen's section: Zhaozhou speaks the imperative to each monk; this witness reverses their order before the steward's follow-up.

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔趙州住院，有僧參次，州云：『上座曾到這裡麼？』僧云：『不曾到。』州云：『吃茶去。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xuzhou Xing (虛舟省禪師語錄), in Xuzhou Xing's retelling of the case: the quoted speaker of the imperative is Zhaozhou Congshen, and the alternate graph for 'drink' marks this as spelling-family evidence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問古人道前三三後三三意如何。師曰。汝名什麼。曰某甲。師曰。喫茶去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), in the section on Zifu Zhensui of Jizhou: Zifu asks the questioner's name and then answers the question with 'go drink tea.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 一切法無差，雲門胡餅趙州茶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), spoken by Xuefeng Sihui in an upper-hall verse: he says all phenomena do not differ and pairs the established allusions 'Yunmen's flatbread' and 'Zhaozhou's tea.' The phrase itself is absent, so this is allusion-family evidence. Xuefeng Sihui is source-attested but awaits the deferred roster expansion.

Occurrences.Kwic: 州曰：喫茶去。院主問：和尚為甚曾到也喫茶去，不曾到也喫茶去？州喚院主，主應諾。州曰：喫茶去。保福展云：趙州慣得其便。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Raising of Old Cases of the School (宗門拈古彙集), in Zhaozhou Congshen's section: Zhaozhou speaks all three exact imperatives; the steward asks why, and the later comment by Baofu Congzhan begins only after the final phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 山僧尋常秖道喫茶去今日也道喫茶去會盡諸方五味禪何似山僧喫茶去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), in Foyan Qingyuan's recorded sayings: Foyan says that he usually says 'go drink tea,' says it again that day, and repeats it after asking how the five-flavored Chan of other places compares.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，眾纔集，便曰：喫茶去。或時眾集，便曰：珍重。或時眾集，便曰：歇。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Record of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), in Baizhang Daoheng's section: when the assembly gathers, Baizhang Daoheng immediately says 'go drink tea'; on other occasions he instead says 'take care' or 'rest.' Baizhang Daoheng is source-attested but awaits the deferred roster expansion.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是古佛家風？師云：蒲團草座。僧曰：若遇客來，將何祇對？師云：喫茶去。僧曰：昔日趙州，今日和尚。師云：錯。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp (建中靖國續燈錄), under the source heading 'Chan Master Cheng of Great Mount Gui in Tanzhou' (潭州大溈山承禪師): asked how he receives a guest, Daweishan Cheng says 'go drink tea'; when the monk equates him with Zhaozhou, he answers, 'Wrong.' The source-attested name is preserved pending the deferred roster review.
